description.narrative:
The country framework that follows UNDAP II in Tanzania is called the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2022-2027 and was launched by mid 2022. Just as the UNDAP II, the UNSDCF is designed to strengthen the coherence and effectiveness of the UN system at national level and contribute to Tanzania's work for sustainable poverty reduction and the realization of human rights. The embassy's assessment is that inter-agency coordination functions remain as important resources for coordinated and coherent work of the UN Country Team implementing the UNSDCF, efficient implementation of the "Leaving No One Behind" (LNOB) commitment and the UNs overall programmatic and policy coherence. Effective interagency coordination is also assessed as important in ensuring a successful bridging between the UNDAP II framework and the UNSDCF.
To ensure continuity of key interagency processes, this appraisal suggests that Sweden will continue to support the UN in maintaining three of the previously four funded positions throughout 2023. The positions will enable uninterrupted support to the UN Programme Coordination Group (PCG), Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Group (MEL), and the Gender Equality and Women Empowerment and Human Rights Coordination Mechanism. The three positions to be supported are: - Results Based Management Specialist (housed at the RCO) - Gender and LNOB Specialist (housed at UNW) - Womens Political Participation and Leadership Coordinator (housed at UNW).
Key expected achievements by the three financed positions during the agreement period will include: - final reporting on the One UN Fund under the UNDAP II, - joint reflections with the government on the results of the first year of the UNSDCF, - joint planning with the integration of the LNOB, gender equality and women's empowerment and human rights principles in the UN's work, - coordination of coherent implementation.
The focus areas of the proposed positions are relevant to priorities set out in the strategy for Swedish development cooperation with Tanzania 2020-2024 and its result areas 'Human rights, democracy, the rule of law and gender equality' and 'Inclusive economic development'.

The United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) for Tanzania 2022 ­2027 is the new cooperation framework rolled out as part of the UN Development System Reform in Tanzania. The UNSDCF was co-­designed by the UN System and the Government of Tanzania (Mainland and Zanzibar) in consultation with a broad range of stakeholders.
The role of inter­agency coordination functions are important resources for coordinated and coherent work of the UN Country Team implementing the UNSDCF, efficient implementation of the "Leaving No One Behind" (LNOB) commitment and the UN’s overall programmatic and policy coherence in supporting Tanzania's sustainable poverty reduction and realization of human rights.
Effective inter­agency coordination is also assessed as important in ensuring a successful bridging between the previous country framework United Nations Development Assistance Plan II (UNDAP II) and the UNSDCF. To ensure continuity of key inter­agency processes, Sweden will support the UN to maintain three key positions throughout 2023. The three positions to be supported are: i) Results Based Management Specialist (housed at the RCO), ii) Gender and LNOB Specialist (housed at UNW), iii) Women’s Political Participation and Leadership Coordinator (housed at UNW).

United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) för Tanzania 2022–2027 är det nya landprogram som FN implementerar som del av FN:s reformagenda i Tanzania. UNSDCF utformades gemensamt av FN och Tanzanias regering (fastlandet och Zanzibar) i samråd med en bred mängd intressenter.
Samordningsfunktioner mellan FN­-organen är viktiga resurser för ett samordnat och sammanhängande arbete i FN:s genomförande av UNSDCF, effektivt genomförande av åtagandet kring att ingen ska lämnas utanför i uppfyllandet av de globala målen ("Leaving No One Behind", LNOB) samt FN: s övergripande programmatiska och politiska samstämmighet i stödet till en hållbar fattigdomsminskning och förverkligandet av de mänskliga rättigheterna i Tanzania. Effektiv samordning mellan organen bedöms också vara viktigt för att säkerställa en sömlös övergång mellan landprogrammen UNDAP II och UNSDCF.
Sverige fortsätter därför stödja FN till att behålla tre av tidigare fyra nyckelpositioner under det andra halvåret av 2023: i)­ Results Based Management Specialist (placerad hos Resident Coordinator Office), ii)­ Gender and LNOB Specialist (placerad hos UN Women), iii) Women’s Political Participation and Leadership Coordinator (placerad hos UN Women).

The strategic, catalytic, ear-marked support from Sweden was used to fund three key positions at the UN in Tanzania, which lacked funding due to the transition from the UNDAP II to the UNSDCF. The specific positions were:
- Results-Based Management (RBM) specialist (based in the Resident Coordinator's Office)
- Gender and LNOB Specialist (based at UN Women)
- Womens Political Participation and Leadership Coordinator (also based at UN Women).
The RBM specialist at the Resident Coordinators Office coordinated inputs from 24 UN agencies and supported major UNSDCF milestones, including annual reviews and the development of Joint Work Plans for 2022/23 and 2023/24. The UN also updated the Common Country Analysis in 2023 and advanced the localization of the SDG Output Indicator Framework. The RBM function strengthened UN staff capacity in RBM, Leave No One Behind (LNOB) principles, and human rightsbased approaches (HRBA), and improved knowledge sharing through a consolidated repository of studies and surveys.
Significant achievements included the completion and endorsement of the UNSDCF Joint Work Plans for 2022/23 and 2023/24, the publication of the UNCT 2022/23 report, and the update of the UN Common Country Analysis in 2023. The RBM function also advanced SDG localization through implementation of the SDG Output Indicator Framework and strengthened monitoring, evaluation, and learning capacities across agencies. Through the UNSDCF MEL Group, around 30 UN staff increased their practical understanding of RBM principles and the integration of Leave No One Behind (LNOB) and Human RightsBased Approaches. A consolidated repository of studies and surveys under the cooperation framework was also established.
The Gender and LNOB Specialist and Womens Political Participation and Leadership Coordinator based at UN Women advanced gender-responsive planning and budgeting (GRB) within government systems. Key achievements include the establishment of GRB coordination mechanisms led by the Ministry of Finance, strengthened GRB capacity among 55 government officials, and integration of GRB into the national and Zanzibar 2024/25 budget guidelines. Sector ministries in Zanzibar have begun mainstreaming GRB in priority areas such as education, agriculture, and the blue economy. The mechanism also provided secretariat functions to the UNCT Gender Equality and Human Rights Coordination Mechanism and strengthened capacity of UN programme staff on the Gender Equality Marker. Annual reporting under the UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard informed progress and guided actions for a new comprehensive assessment scheduled for 2024.
Further achievements that the positions contributed to included the provision of secretariat support to the UNCT Gender Equality and Human Rights Coordination Mechanism, enabling coordinated UN action on Gender Equality and Womens Empowerment (GEWE) and human rights issues. Training on the Gender Equality Marker (GEM) strengthened UN agencies tracking of investments in gender equality, with 20 programme staff completing training and undertaking quality assurance reviews for the 2023/24 Joint Annual Workplans. In addition, the 2023 UNCTSWAP Gender Equality Scorecard report was produced, highlighting progress and areas for improvement, and preparations were initiated for a new comprehensive assessment in 2024 to strengthen accountability for gender mainstreaming under the UNSDCF.
In its final year, the overall Fund, which Sida's support contributed to, achieved the following:
• Community-based approaches improved access to WASH, education, and protection services:160,000 individuals were screened for TB, 8,000 women received antenatal care, 6,000 girls received dignity kits, and adolescent health services reached over 21,000 youth in the Kigoma region. Birth registration rose to 65.5% in 2024 from 10% in 2022 in Kigoma. • 2,569 enterprises were formalized, over TZS 164 million in loans was accessed through savings groups, and more than 800 women and youth adopted micro-irrigation technologies. Farmers aggregated and sold 100MT of beans at premium prices, benefiting over 300 smallholders. • Over 487,000 mangroves were planted, 29,000 farmers trained in climate-smart agriculture, and 17 schools transitioned to clean energy. Clean cooking technologies reached 3,500 people, improving health and reducing deforestation. • Key frameworks for gender equality and human rights were strengthened. Local knowledge and capacities on trafficking prevention, legal aid, and freedom of expression were enhanced.
